details: Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency, fell to its lowest level in two years on Friday, November 20, 2026, dropping to $55,830. This decline was attributed to investor worries over stretched valuations in artificial intelligence stocks, rising borrowing costs, and broader risk aversion in financial markets. US stock indexes also experienced their steepest weekly decline since April 2025. Bitcoin briefly rebounded over 8% to around $59,952 on Saturday.
title: Bitcoin Plunges to Two-Year Low Amid AI Concerns and Risk Aversion

details: On November 20, 2026, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde emphasized the urgent need for the EU to accelerate the implementation of its MiCA regulation to establish a unified market for tokenized assets. Lagarde warned that delays could lead to fragmentation as competing blockchain platforms develop incompatible standards. The ECB's Pontes platform, launched in September 2026, already facilitates wholesale tokenized securities in central bank money, and the ECB is inviting financial institutions to participate in its Appia initiative to further develop tokenized financial infrastructure.
title: ECB Urges Swift EU Action on Unified Tokenized Asset Market

details: Kristalina Georgieva, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), cautioned on November 20, 2026, that further corrections in the prices of artificial intelligence-related financial assets are likely. She noted that current investor optimism regarding AI might be excessive and that while a major downturn is not anticipated, additional market adjustments could make the market more resilient. Georgieva also highlighted concerns about the rapid expansion of "circular financing arrangements" in the AI chip sector, which have reached approximately $1 trillion, with a growing reliance on debt funding.
title: IMF Warns of Further Correction in AI-Related Financial Assets

details: Despite Congress failing to advance the CLARITY Act, a key crypto market structure bill, US crypto regulation is progressing through federal agencies. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) finalized the first federal rule for payment stablecoin issuers on October 21, 2026, which will take effect on January 18, 2027, alongside the GENIUS Act stablecoin law. This indicates a continued push for regulatory clarity, even without comprehensive legislative action.
title: US Crypto Regulation Advances Through Agencies as Congress Stalls
